title: Hedged-reserve tier routing: quota smoothing and soft-reserve for free/paid/enterprise
creator: Marina Gomez
description: Problem: Free, paid, and enterprise plans share physical capacity in Hosted and Dedicated modes. Under spiky demand free-tier traffic can starve paid customers if we naively admit requests based purely on arrival order, yet overly strict reservations reduce utilization and raise cost. This ticket defines a hedged-reserve, quota-smoothing routing mechanism that balances utilization with plan guarantees and provides graceful degradation to cheaper model variants or regional fallbacks.
goals: Guarantee minimal free-tier responsiveness without unduly impacting paid/enterprise latency SLOs
Maintain high overall GPU utilization (>70% target) via opportunistic borrowing and smoothing
Provide deterministic fallback paths (cheaper model variant, different region, or delayed admission) when soft-reserve thresholds hit
Expose metrics and controls in Console for reserve sizes, smoothing window, and preemption behavior
non_goals: Replace full billing/plan entitlement system (this ticket focuses on routing behavior only)
Implement new plan billing discounts or refunds on degraded quality
design_summary: Introduce a 3-layer admission controller: (1) Per-plan soft-reserve buckets sized by historical peak and business policy, implemented as token-leaky windows; (2) Opportunistic borrow: unused reserve capacity decays into a global opportunistic pool that higher tiers can use but will be preemptible; (3) Deterministic fallback policies that map admitted requests to cheaper model variants or cross-region endpoints when reserve thresholds exceed configured degradation curves. Each admission decision emits deterministic reason codes for observability (e.g., ACCEPT, BORROWED_OPPORTUNISTIC, FALLBACK_MODEL, DEMOTED_REGION, THROTTLED).
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests covering reserve accounting, borrow/repay cycles, and preemption events
Synthetic load test demonstrates paid-tier p95 latency no worse than current baseline under mixed 2x spike while free-tier p95 remains < 500ms for at least 70% of requests
Console surface shows live reserve utilization, opportunistic pool size, and recent preemption events
Canary rollout (10% traffic) passes reliability gates for 48h in hosted region-us-west1
implementation_notes: Admission controller will be implemented as a modular layer in router service (router/admission). Keep API backward compatible with current admitRequest(requestMeta) signature and return richer admitOutcome struct (reasonCode string, evictable boolean, targetModel string)
Reserve accounting stored in per-region Redis shard with TTL-based smoothing windows; counters are approximate (use HLL-style decay) to avoid hot keys
Borrowing uses a timestamped ledger so opportunistic tokens are repayable; preemption follows LRU on opportunistic tokens to minimize user disruptions

Fallback model variants should be declared in model catalog with compatibility metadata (semantic-preservation score). Router must prefer same-architecture cheaper variants first before cross-region fallbacks
Add feature flag gate (router.hedged_reserve.enabled) and gradual config knobs in Config Service for reserve sizes and decay rates
safety_and_risks: Risk: aggressive borrowing could cause paid customers to observe intermittent latency spikes if preemption is delayed. Mitigation: strict preemption latency budget and telemetry alerting
Risk: cross-region fallbacks introduce data residency concerns. Mitigation: only use region fallback for customers without strict residency flags; consult RBAC/tenant metadata
Operational risk: new Redis access pattern may increase cost. Mitigation: start with small shard keyspace and monitor key heat
metrics: preemption_count: number of opportunistic evictions per minute
fallback_rate: percent of requests routed to cheaper model or region
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): unit tests + local router integration with simulated Redis ledger - target week 1
Phase 2 (internal canary): enable for internal org and 5% of production traffic behind feature flag - monitor for 72h
Phase 3 (customer canary): opt-in tenants, 10% traffic in us-west1 - run 48h gates
Phase 4 (global): enable in additional regions with metrics validation
